done.why: I died for the second time, staying in the reservoir to see what refilling it would do. I woke up back in the forest with my things scattered again. The thief had already taken my emerald and painting, so I would have had to walk the whole route to the dam a third time. I had seen the dam and river part properly and didn't want to retrace it all again.

about: The white house and the underground empire, centred on Flood Control Dam #3 and the Frigid River. You get the green bubble glowing from the maintenance room, open the sluice gates with a wrench, and the lake drains to a mud flat with a trunk of jewels in it. You pump up a plastic boat and drift down a river that pulls you toward the falls whether you're ready or not. A wordless thief takes your treasures, and death sends you back to the forest while your belongings get tidied away around the house.

ending.what: No real ending. I died twice: once over the waterfall (turn 135) and once washed over the dam while standing in the refilling reservoir (turn 194). Each time I was brought back in the forest.

moments.note: 'kick the mailbox open' got 'You can't see any such thing.' even though the mailbox was right there. The parser doesn't like extra words.
Trying to climb the chimney: 'Only Santa Claus climbs down chimneys.'
The gothic lettering reads 'This space intentionally left blank.'
The troll graciously ate my lunch, then kept attacking me anyway.
The green bubble has 'the patient look of something waiting to be told it may begin.' A lovely clue.
The weight limit called out the sword by name: 'the sword not least of it.'
The wrench on the bolt opened the sluice gates. Very satisfying once the bubble was glowing.
Examining the plastic says instructions 'go on round the back', but 'read plastic' says 'How does one read a pile of plastic?' and I couldn't turn it over or unfold it.
Reservoir South was redescribed as a drained lake with a stream, and an old trunk had turned up in the mud.
The boat inflated, and the label told me how to use it ('Hello, Sailor!').
The Loud Room let me act normally. 'take bar' came back as 'Bar bar ...', and 'echo' changed the acoustics.
Giving the platinum bar to the thief worked. He was 'taken aback by your unexpected generosity'.
Taking the emerald from the buoy cost a turn, and the current carried me over the falls to my death with no extra warning.
The death text was charming: 'somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.'
The gallery's bare hooks and pale rectangles, 'each one exactly the size of something worth having.'
My lost emerald had 'rolled' into the Studio, just as the death message promised.
The chimney has room for 'you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.' A clear rule.
While I dropped the manual to fit up the chimney, the thief robbed me blind of the emerald and painting.
Things I had dropped in the reservoir stayed put. They didn't get scattered like the things I'd been carrying.
Waiting in the refilling reservoir swept me over the dam. The warning had been fair.

wished: To read the instructions printed on the folded plastic, since examining it says they go on round the back
To phrase things with extra words ('kick the mailbox open', 'turn bolt with my bare hands', 'pump up the plastic right here') without getting 'You can't see any such thing'
To turn the guidebook's page past the cut-off tour text
To paddle upstream or steer against the current
To get my emerald and painting back from the thief, or at least to see him coming
To pry the nailed door with the sword, or dig through the cave-ins

lines.line: The engravings translate to "This space intentionally left blank."
lines.why: Funny, and it rewarded me for poking at scenery.

lines.line: It is dark, and has the patient look of something waiting to be told it may begin.
lines.why: A good clue that sent me looking for the buttons.

lines.line: Your belongings, such as they were, have not come with you. The plain things are strewn about the forest and the fields around the house, anything of value has rolled into some dark corner in or under it, and somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: It made death feel gentle and told me where to look. It turned out to be true.

lines.line: Where the stolen paintings hung there are only bare hooks and pale rectangles on the wall, each one exactly the size of something worth having.
lines.why: The best piece of description I read.

lines.line: The chimney has room for you, your lamp and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
lines.why: A clear, fair statement of the limit.

lines.line: The thief is taken aback by your unexpected generosity, but accepts the platinum bar and stops to admire its beauty.
lines.why: My contrary move was handled rather than refused.

fun.why: Opening the dam, inflating the boat and finding the emerald again were all satisfying. Giving the bar to the thief worked. Being robbed and dying to the current took some of the fun out.

engagement.why: The dam's chain of cause and effect kept me pushing. Draining the lake changed the rooms, and the death text promised my things had gone somewhere. Retracing the route after the second death is what made me stop.

difficulty.why: The puzzles were fair once I read closely. The weight limit and the river current were harsh, and the unreadable plastic instructions were a dead end.

interestingness.why: Familiar ground but with fresh touches: the waiting bubble, a Loud Room you can act in, a gentle death that tidies up, and a chimney with a stated limit.

prose.why: The new lines are dry, warm and precise, and they sit well beside the old ones. Parser replies to unusual phrasing were curt ('You can't see any such thing.').
